verdict.rationale: Vercel positions one platform to deploy and scale apps, and its plan tiers keep the same primitives with higher ceilings: Fluid compute scaling, the same function limits with larger Pro/Enterprise maxima, and a 99.99% Enterprise SLA. However, Vercel retired its own Postgres and KV primitives and moved users to Neon and Upstash, which shows core primitives have changed underneath developers. Missing for 10: an explicit documented no-rearchitecting or primitive-stability commitment, independent evidence of prototype-to-massive-scale continuity, and stability of first-party data primitives (Postgres/KV were discontinued).

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the same core APIs and primitives from prototype through massive scale, without rearchitecting or migrating platforms as usage grows

citations.quote: Deploy and scale web applications, APIs, and AI workloads from a Git repository or the Vercel CLI.
Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
300s default, 800s max, up to 1800s (30 minutes) in beta [Pro and Enterprise]
available 99.99% of the time, excluding any Excused Downtime events
